walkthroughs.body_html:
Rural Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rural Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rural Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

mcqs.q: How do rivers transport their load?
options: Rivers transport everything by pushing it along the bottom.
By traction (rolling large stones along the bed), saltation (bouncing smaller pebbles), suspension (carrying fine sediment in the flow) and solution (dissolved minerals).
Rivers can only transport material when they are in flood.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

mcqs.q: Why might managed retreat be more sustainable than building a sea wall?
options: Sea walls are expensive, deflect erosion elsewhere and reflect wave energy worsening beach loss; managed retreat works with natural processes, creates habitat and is cheaper long-term.
Sea walls always solve coastal erosion problems permanently.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
